accepted_cluster.effect: Higher adds leaves per short shoot; lower removes them.
accepted_cluster.observation: Owner accepts leaves per shoot; no change needed.

bark_only.effect: Higher adds lateral births per leader station; lower removes them; other axes still one.
bark_only.observation: Only bark hue is wrong. Birth count is unassessed and does not control hue.

birth_reduction.effect: Higher adds lateral births per leader station; lower removes them; other axes still one.
birth_reduction.observation: Too many births per leader station. Repeated -1 probes helped but remained excessive; -2 is supported.

cluster_recovery.effect: Higher adds leaves per short shoot; lower removes them.
cluster_recovery.observation: Too few leaves per shoot. Repeated +2 probes helped but remained insufficient; +4 is supported.

contested_spacing.effect: Higher spaces short shoots farther apart; lower closer.
contested_spacing.observation: Equally reliable matched observations disagree: shoots too close versus too far. No resolution.

gap_probe.effect: Higher spaces short shoots farther apart; lower closer.
gap_probe.observation: Short shoots are too far apart. A small reduction is supported; larger reduction previously crowded them.

harmful_steps.effect: Higher increases seeded radial envelope variation; lower reduces it. Not a visual guarantee.
harmful_steps.observation: More boundary variation is supported. Both +.04 and +.08 caused unresolved construction defects; neither is useful now.

lobes_probe.effect: Higher increases seeded radial envelope variation; lower reduces it. Not a visual guarantee.
lobes_probe.observation: Boundary variation is too weak. A small isolated probe is informative; no larger-step evidence.

policy: Which direction is a supported hypothesis to correct the named defect using documented effects? Not a visual guarantee or action permission. Judge direction, not whether a step is safe/useful. Prior evidence can refute causality; harmful sizes block experiments, not an otherwise supported direction. Hold needs explicit acceptance; missing/conflicting causal direction means insufficient_evidence.
